task_description: Verify the crates.io trusted-publishing path against production and fix a latent workflow bug: both release.yml invocations placed the top-level --root flag after the subcommand, which argparse rejects with exit 2
verification: Ran the exact workflow commands: broken form exits 2, corrected form exits 0
cargo publish --dry-run --locked on a real workspace crate: packages, verifies, uploads (dry run)
Workspace-inherited version (version.workspace = true) resolves correctly at publish time
--locked works without a committed Cargo.lock (library-repo policy)
New contract test fails on the previous workflow and passes on the fix (non-vacuous)
Pinned crates-io-auth-action SHA 3268eb41 matches upstream tag v1.0.6 exactly
notes: The publish job has never executed in production: every release run predates it, no crate is on crates.io, and the allowlist ships empty. The bug was therefore latent, not a regression. Fixed at source on PR #501 and documented that the release environment must be created manually, because GitHub auto-creates a named environment with no protection rules.
